Implement a set of ALREADY-DIAGNOSED fixes in /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (the Nxeon migration engine). Edit the file directly. After editing you MUST run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until it is CLEAN (exit 0), and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts` (should stay green). Do NOT run the worker, do NOT deploy, do NOT commit, do NOT touch any other file. Report exactly what you changed with final line numbers.

## Context already in place (do not redo)
I already added, on the `SrcContainer` inspect, two captured fields: `configFiles: string` (the compose `com.docker.compose.project.config_files` label — comma-joined absolute paths in the source's `-f` order) and `composeWd: string` (the `com.docker.compose.project.working_dir` label). The scan template (~line 1038), the type, the default-init, and the parser cases are DONE. Verify they exist (grep `configFiles`, `composeWd`) but do not re-add them.

`srcContainers` is defined at ~line 4500 (`const srcContainers = inv.probed ? inv.containers : [];`) and is in scope in the compose bring-up region (~5325-5430). Helpers available in that scope: `sh(conn,cmd,timeout?)`, `shOk(conn,cmd,timeout?)`, `clean(str,max)`, `cleanLines(str,max)`, `validPath(p)`, `validImageRef(r)`, `isLocalImageRef(r)`, `ensureImage(conn,ref,local,onSource,priv,say)→Promise<{status:"present"|"pulled"|"loaded"|"failed";detail:string}>`, `onSource(cmd)`, `priv`, `parseComposeRequiredVars`, `pruneDocker`, `human`, `isEnospc`, `lastErrorLine`, `BUILTIN_NETWORKS` (Set), `report(pct,phase,line)`, `push({step,status,detail})`, `work`, `composeCmd`, `TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_MS`. Do NOT invent helpers.

## The current code (read it first): `composeEnvFor` (~5325-5357), `composeFileArg` (~5358-5361), and the `if (plan.composeDirs.length) { … }` loop (~5363-5418). Understand it before editing.

## FIX 1 — Replay the source's real compose `-f` file list (THE serving fix)
Problem: the engine brings up only ONE guessed compose file, so an app whose tier lives in `docker-compose.prod.yml` never starts (only base/infra services come up; the domain doesn't serve).
- Before `composeEnvFor`, build `const srcComposeFiles = new Map<string,string[]>()` from `srcContainers`: for each container with non-empty `composeWd` and `configFiles`, key = `composeWd` with trailing slashes stripped, value = `configFiles.split(",").map(trim).filter(validPath)`; keep the first non-empty per key.
- Change `composeEnvFor(dir)` to return `{ args, missing, envFile, composeFile, composeFiles: string[], fileArg: string }`. Logic: look up `srcComposeFiles.get(dir without trailing slash)`; keep only files that pass `test -f` on the target; if ≥1, use them and set `explicit=true`. Else fall back to the EXISTING single-file detection (`for f in docker-compose.yml … ; do [ -f ${dir}/$f ]…`) as a 1-element list. If still none, return empty shape. Compute `fileArg`: if `explicit || composeFiles.length>1 || the single file is a NON-default name`, then `composeFiles.map(cf=>\`-f ${cf} \`).join("")`; else `""` (a lone default-named file keeps auto-loading its override as before). Scan required vars across ALL `composeFiles` (join with spaces in the existing grep), not just one. Keep `composeFile: composeFiles[0] ?? ""` for compatibility.
- Replace every `composeFileArg(ce.composeFile)` call in the loop (there are ~4: the missing-vars hint, the `up -d`, the `ps` count, the failed-hint `logs`) with `ce.fileArg`. You may leave `composeFileArg` defined/unused or delete it (no `noUnusedLocals`).

## FIX 2 — Honest N-of-M verdict (no false "running" on partial bring-up), v1-safe, with poll
Replace the current `sleep 10` + `ps --status running -q | wc -l` + `if(runningCount>0)` verdict block. New logic:
- `expected` = `${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}${ce.args}config --services | wc -l` (works on v1+v2).
- A `runningNow()` helper that lists project container ids via `${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}${ce.args}ps -q` (v1+v2 safe — do NOT use `ps --status`, which errors on compose v1) then counts `true` from `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' <ids>`.
- Poll with backoff `for (const wait of [10,12,15,18]) { sleep wait; runningCount=await runningNow(); if (expected>0 && runningCount>=expected) break; }` (DB-init-then-app stacks exceed a single 10s wait).
- Verdict: if `runningCount>0 && (expected===0 || runningCount>=expected)` → status "running", detail `${runningCount}/${expected} service(s) running` (or just count if expected 0). Else if `runningCount>0` → status "failed", detail `only ${runningCount} of ${expected} service(s) stayed up — the rest crash-looped or exited. Check: cd ${dir} && ${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}${ce.args}logs`. Else (0) → keep the EXISTING enospc/lastErrorLine "containers did not stay up" failed branch. Preserve the enospc-retry logic above it.

## FIX 3 — External-network pre-pass (mailserver: "network X declared as external, but could not be found")
Right after the `Bringing up N project(s)` report and BEFORE the `for (const dir …)` loop, add a best-effort `try{…}catch{}` pre-pass: across all `plan.composeDirs`, for each project's compose file(s) (use `srcComposeFiles.get(dir)` if present, else the default candidate names on disk), scan the top-level `networks:` block with awk (`awk 'BEGIN{inn=0} /^networks:[[:space:]]*$/{inn=1;next} inn&&/^[^[:space:]]/{inn=0} inn{print}' <cf>`). For each 2-space-indented network key: if it has `external: true` → its name is the `name:` override else the key; else it's created by that project as `<project>_<key>` where project = dir basename lowercased alnum. Collect `externalRefs` and `willCreate` (skip `BUILTIN_NETWORKS`). Then for each `externalRefs` name NOT in `willCreate` and matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$/`: `docker network inspect <net> >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker network create <net> >/dev/null 2>&1` (idempotent) and report "Ensured shared network <net> exists." Never pre-create a name a migrated project owns (avoids compose label-mismatch).

## FIX 4 — Compose image pre-flight (studionexis/backend "pull access denied")
Inside the loop, AFTER the missing-vars check and BEFORE `up -d`: enumerate the project's images via `${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}${ce.args}config --images`, filter `validImageRef`, dedupe. For each not already present (`docker image inspect <ref>` fails): call `ensureImage(conn, ref, isLocalImageRef(ref), onSource, priv, l=>report(75,"Starting containers…",l))`. If it returns `status==="failed"`: for a local ref → block with "built on the old server but could not be transferred (<detail>)"; for a registry ref → block with an honest "needs registry credentials: run 'docker login' … then cd <dir> && <composeCmd> <fileArg><args>up -d". On block: `push` a `failed` "Compose up <dir>" step with that message and `continue` (skip `up`). This makes compose reuse the transferred local image instead of trying to pull it.

## FIX 5 — Duplicate container_name across projects (soulpilates-staging "container name already in use")
Inside the loop, before `up -d` (after FIX 4 is fine): keep a `const claimedNames = new Map<string,string>()` declared ONCE before the loop. For the current project, read literal `container_name:` values from `ce.composeFiles` via `grep -hE '^[[:space:]]*container_name:' … | sed -E` (strip key, trailing comments, surrounding quotes). If any value is already in `claimedNames`, `push` a `skipped` "Compose up <dir>" step naming the clashing container and the owning dir (explain container_name is absolute; these are the same app's prod+staging; run on separate host or give unique names; give the manual `up` command) and `continue`. Otherwise register every name → dir in `claimedNames` and proceed. Order the checks so a project that fails FIX4 image block does NOT claim names (i.e. do the container_name claim only for projects you actually bring up — simplest: do FIX5 check+claim immediately before the `up -d`).

## FIX 6 — Standalone named-volume empty-data guard (silent DB data-loss → false "running")
This is in the STANDALONE container path (~5490-5540, search `docker volume create`, `buildRunCommand`, the bind-mount `missing`/`test -e ${b.src}` refusal). Currently bind mounts are guarded (a container whose bind source didn't arrive is refused) but NAMED VOLUMES are not: `docker volume create ${v.name}` fabricates an EMPTY volume and the container boots against a blank datadir and reads Running=true. Add, before starting a standalone container that mounts named volumes (`p.volumes`), a guard: for each named volume, if the target volume's data dir is empty (`find /var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data -mindepth 1 -print -quit` returns nothing) AND the source's same volume was non-empty (best-effort: skip this sub-check if you cannot determine it cheaply — but DO refuse on empty target volume for a container whose image is a known stateful engine: postgres/mysql/mariadb/mongo), then push a `copied`/`failed` step naming the volume ("its data volume <name> did not migrate — starting it would run against an empty database; copy /var/lib/docker/volumes/<name> from the old server, then start it") and `continue` instead of starting. Mirror the existing bind-mount refusal style. Keep it conservative: do not refuse a stateless container just because a cache volume is empty — gate the hard refusal on stateful DB images, and for other empty named volumes emit a WARNING step but still start. Cite the exact lines you change.

## Constraints
- Preserve ALL existing honest gates (missing-secrets refusal, bind-mount-missing refusal, enospc retry). Do not force-start anything.
- Every new shell command must be safe under the existing quoting (single-quoted `sh -c '…'` wrappers like the current code). Match the file's style.
- Keep changes surgical and within the compose/standalone bring-up region. Do not refactor unrelated code.
- FINISH ONLY when `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and the consolidate test passes. Report final line numbers + a concise diff summary per fix.
